svg.title: Docker & Containers
svg.desc: Docker & Containers. Package an app and its dependencies as an image and run it as an isolated process: layers, registries, namespaces, cgroups. Step 1, Where it sits: CI builds catalog:1.4.2 once; laptop, staging and production pull the same digest from Amazon ECR. Step 2, Layers and the cache: Only the app code changed: BuildKit builds one new layer, and push and pull move only that layer. Step 3, Running a container: docker run: runc starts node as PID 1 in its own namespaces, in a cgroup capped at 0.5 CPU, 512 MiB. Step 4, Limits and trade-offs: catalog-2 hits 512 MiB: OOM-killed (exit 137). Shared kernel; the writable layer is temporary.

g.text: CI builds catalog:1.4.2 once; laptop, staging and production pull the same digest from Amazon ECR.
Only the app code changed: BuildKit builds one new layer, and push and pull move only that layer.
docker run: runc starts node as PID 1 in its own namespaces, in a cgroup capped at 0.5 CPU, 512 MiB.
catalog-2 hits 512 MiB: OOM-killed (exit 137). Shared kernel; the writable layer is temporary.
one in every environment, same image
Pulled by digest: the image tested in staging is the image in production.
shared by every container on host-1
shared kernel: weaker isolation than a VM
CI builds catalog:1.4.2 once and pushes it to Amazon ECR, where the tag points to a digest: sha256:9f2c…, a hash of the image manifest.
Laptop, staging and production pull that digest, not the tag, so the image that passed in staging is, byte for byte, what runs in production.
Each RUN, COPY or ADD saves its file changes as a read-only layer named by a hash of its content; the node:24 build stages are left behind.
Only src/ changed, so BuildKit re-runs the three steps that depend on it and takes the rest from its cache. Push and pull move just the new layer.
A CONTAINER IS AN ISOLATED PROCESS
dockerd asks containerd, and runc starts node as PID 1 in new pid, net, mnt, uts, ipc and cgroup namespaces, so it sees only its own world.
Its cgroup caps it: cpu.max 50000 100000 (0.5 CPU), memory.max 512 MiB. Writes land in a thin writable layer; image layers and kernel are shared.
catalog-2 hit memory.max, so the kernel's OOM killer sent it SIGKILL (exit code 137). Removing it deletes its writable layer and all in it.
one shared kernel: weaker isolation than a VM
keep state in volumes or a database
scan, sign and pin images by digest
